question: What are the 100 most significant and influential galleries in Venice, ranked in order? If less than 100 significant galleries exist, provide the complete list of significant galleries.

galleries.name: Victoria Miro Venice
galleries.address_hint: Il Capricorno, San Marco 1994, Calle Drio la Chiesa

notes.anthropic: Venice outpost of the London mega-gallery, in the historic Il Capricorno space; shows Grayson Perry, Chris Ofili, Yayoi Kusama and others, and is the city's strongest international commercial programme.
notes.openai: The Venetian branch of an internationally prominent gallery, bringing major represented artists and a blue-chip programme to a permanent, seasonally operated space.

notes.anthropic: The most ambitious Venetian-owned contemporary gallery, with a large Giudecca warehouse space, a research-driven programme and consistent Italian art-fair presence.
notes.openai: One of Venice’s most respected contemporary galleries, known for conceptually oriented artists and sustained institutional visibility.

notes.anthropic: Paris–Venice gallery showing an international roster of conceptual and performance-based artists; regular at Artissima, Art Brussels and Paris fairs.
notes.openai: A leading Venice–Paris gallery with a rigorous international programme, strong institutional links and regular art-fair participation.

notes.anthropic: Rigorous programme bridging Italian post-war abstraction and younger conceptual practices; a fixture of Venice's Biennale-season calendar and of Italian fairs.
notes.openai: A highly regarded programme combining established and emerging Italian and international artists, supported by fairs and museum collaborations.

notes.anthropic: Restored palazzo opened 2024 with permanent site-specific commissions (Sterling Ruby, Urs Fischer, Lee Ufan) and a residency; instantly a major Venice venue.
notes.openai: An ambitious new cultural hub commissioning major site-specific works from internationally recognized contemporary artists.

galleries.name: Ocean Space (TBA21–Academy)
galleries.address_hint: Chiesa di San Lorenzo, Campo San Lorenzo, Castello 5069

notes.anthropic: TBA21–Academy's commissioning platform in a deconsecrated church, pairing major artist commissions with ocean research; internationally the most-discussed non-Biennale venue in the city.
notes.openai: TBA21–Academy’s influential platform for ambitious art, ecology and ocean-focused commissions in the monumental Church of San Lorenzo.

notes.anthropic: Slovenian exhibition centre turned experimental gallery and school platform; long history of Central/Eastern European and emerging Italian shows.
notes.openai: A long-running experimental gallery that has helped launch emerging practices while connecting exhibitions with curatorial research and education.

galleries.name: Fondazione Bevilacqua La Masa
galleries.address_hint: Piazza San Marco 71/c; Palazzetto Tito, Dorsoduro 2826

notes.anthropic: Founded 1898, the city's historic incubator for emerging artists, with studios, an annual open call and two public exhibition spaces.
notes.openai: A historic Venetian institution whose exhibitions, studios and annual young-artists programme have shaped generations of local contemporary practice.

notes.anthropic: The reference gallery for contemporary art in glass, working with international artists and museums since 1992.
notes.openai: An internationally recognized specialist in contemporary art using glass, with an influential programme extending well beyond traditional Murano practice.

notes.anthropic: Artist's foundation in a Renzo Piano-adapted salt warehouse; exhibitions of Vedova alongside leading international contemporary artists.
notes.openai: Preserves Vedova’s legacy while mounting serious exhibitions and cross-generational dialogues in spaces designed with Renzo Piano.

galleries.name: Berengo Studio / Fondazione Berengo
galleries.address_hint: Fondamenta Vetrai 109/A and Campiello della Pescheria, Murano

notes.anthropic: Furnace, gallery and foundation behind 'Glasstress', which has brought hundreds of major contemporary artists to work in Murano glass.
notes.openai: A crucial bridge between contemporary art and Murano glass, internationally influential through artist collaborations and the recurring Glasstress project.

names.openai: Berengo Studio and Fondazione Berengo Art Space

notes.anthropic: Free corporate exhibition space presenting works from the Fondation Louis Vuitton collection and solo projects by internationally established artists.
notes.openai: A compact but prominent corporate cultural venue presenting commissioned projects and exhibitions connected with the Fondation Louis Vuitton collection.

notes.anthropic: Independent, occupation-born collective space for politically engaged art, activism and experimental programming; a critical counter-voice to the Biennale economy.
notes.openai: An artist-run and activist cultural space influential for politically engaged art, commons-based organization and critical debate around the Biennale.

notes.anthropic: Independent space in a former brewery known for design-adjacent, experimental and youth-driven exhibitions and collaborations.
notes.openai: An agile nonprofit space supporting experimental exhibitions, publishing, design and interdisciplinary projects in a former industrial setting.

notes.anthropic: Long-running photography gallery in the Ghetto, run by Živa Kraus since 1979, with a strong documentary and Central European emphasis.
notes.openai: Founded by Živa Kraus, this pioneering photography and contemporary-art gallery has sustained an independent programme since the late 1970s.

galleries.name: Galleria d'Arte Contini
galleries.address_hint: Calle dello Spezier 2765 and San Marco 2288, Campo Santo Stefano

notes.anthropic: The city's largest commercial operation, with modern masters and blue-chip contemporary names plus high-visibility public installations.
notes.openai: A longstanding commercial gallery with multiple Venetian premises, a recognizable roster and an international clientele for modern and contemporary art.

notes.anthropic: Producer of architecture and art exhibitions and Biennale collateral events, with a project space on the Giudecca waterfront.
notes.openai: A well-established Venetian producer and exhibition platform responsible for numerous international contemporary-art projects across the city.

galleries.name: Beatrice Burati Anderson Art Space & Gallery

notes.anthropic: Curator-run gallery with a lively programme of emerging Italian and international artists and Biennale-season collateral projects.
notes.openai: A curator-led space supporting interdisciplinary and socially attentive contemporary practices through exhibitions and special projects.

names.anthropic: Beatrice Burati Anderson Art Space & Gallery
names.openai: Beatrice Burati Anderson Art Space & Gallery

notes.anthropic: Established Venetian dealer of postwar and contemporary Italian art, active since the 1990s with a busy exhibition calendar.
notes.openai: A longstanding commercial gallery with a dependable programme of Italian and international modern and contemporary artists.

galleries.name: CREA Cantieri del Contemporaneo
galleries.address_hint: Giudecca 211, ex convento dei SS. Cosma e Damiano

notes.anthropic: Studios, residencies and exhibition halls in a former convent; a hub for the Giudecca Art District and local artist community.
notes.openai: A multidisciplinary cultural centre providing production and exhibition space for independent art, performance and community-led projects.

notes.anthropic: Large independent hall near Fondamente Nove hosting national pavilions, collateral events and ambitious guest-curated shows.
notes.openai: A restored former workshop and chapel used for substantial contemporary exhibitions, installations and cultural projects.

notes.anthropic: Exhibition centre opened 2025 on the piano nobile above Piazza San Marco, programming international art and architecture shows.
notes.openai: A major new exhibition centre whose scale, central location and interdisciplinary international programme give it immediate institutional importance.

galleries.name: European Cultural Centre (Palazzo Mora / Palazzo Bembo)

notes.anthropic: Runs the sprawling 'Personal Structures' exhibitions across two palazzi; hugely visible during Biennale years, if divisive critically.
notes.openai: A large international exhibition platform operating Palazzo Mora, Palazzo Bembo and outdoor sites, especially visible during Biennale seasons.

names.anthropic: European Cultural Centre (Palazzo Mora / Palazzo Bembo)

galleries.name: V–A–C Zattere
galleries.address_hint: Fondamenta Zattere al Ponte Longo, Dorsoduro 1401

notes.openai: The Venetian venue of V–A–C Foundation, notable for large-scale, research-led exhibitions and international institutional partnerships.

notes.anthropic: Family gallery in Piazza San Marco since 1967, mixing historic Venetian modernism with contemporary sculpture and glass.
notes.openai: A prominent family-run gallery active since the 1960s, maintaining a highly visible programme of modern and contemporary art.
The Venetian branch of the established Gstaad gallery presents internationally collected contemporary artists in a historic palazzo.

notes.anthropic: Curatorially sharp gallery mixing modern estates with young international artists; a key stop for the visiting art world during Biennale openings.

galleries.name: Tommaso Calabro Venezia
galleries.address_hint: Palazzo Donà Brusa, Campo San Polo

notes.openai: An influential Milan–Venice gallery combining postwar rediscoveries, artist estates and carefully selected contemporary positions.
A young nonprofit platform with an internationally oriented programme of emerging and mid-career artists, residencies and commissioned exhibitions.

galleries.name: The Pool NYC at Palazzo Cesari Marchesi

notes.openai: An international gallery platform staging ambitious exhibitions in a permanent Venetian palazzo, often around the Biennale calendar.

names.openai: The Pool NYC at Palazzo Cesari Marchesi

notes.anthropic: Industrial site inside the Arsenale hosting large-scale sculpture, national participations and collateral exhibitions since the 1990s.
notes.openai: An unusual Arsenale venue and sculpture garden with a long record of hosting contemporary installations and Biennale-adjacent projects.

notes.anthropic: Small waterfront gallery central to the Giudecca Art District, showing emerging and mid-career Italian artists.
notes.openai: A durable independent gallery presenting contemporary art, photography and projects attentive to Venice’s social and architectural context.

galleries.name: Le Stanze del Vetro
galleries.address_hint: Fondazione Giorgio Cini, Isola di San Giorgio Maggiore

notes.anthropic: Free exhibition space devoted to 20th-century and contemporary glass, with scholarly, museum-quality shows and a permanent study centre.

notes.openai: The Venice branch of a longstanding Italian gallery dealing in important modern masters alongside established contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Photography- and lens-based gallery next to La Fenice, showing international names and Venice-specific commissions.

notes.openai: An internationally connected gallery distinguished in Venice by its sustained focus on contemporary artists from Africa and its diaspora.
An independent space known for focused presentations by emerging international artists and collaborations with galleries and curators.

notes.anthropic: One of Venice's oldest continuously running contemporary galleries (since 1968), with deep roots in the Italian postwar scene.
Fluxus-linked residency and exhibition space continuing the legacy of the New York dealer; small but internationally networked.
Venice branch of the Geneva-based chain; commercially prominent pop and urban-art programme in the San Marco tourist core.
notes.openai: Part of an international commercial network with a highly visible Venice presence and a broad programme of postwar, pop and contemporary work.

galleries.name: Microclima
galleries.address_hint: Serra dei Giardini, Via Giuseppe Garibaldi 1254

notes.anthropic: Curatorial platform in the Giardini's historic greenhouse, producing site-specific projects, talks and artist commissions year-round.

notes.openai: An independent exhibition and residency venue providing sustained visibility for emerging and mid-career international artists.

galleries.name: Nuova Icona
galleries.address_hint: Giudecca; also Oratorio di San Ludovico, Dorsoduro

notes.anthropic: Artist-run association active since 1993, producing exhibitions and Biennale collateral projects in unusual sacred spaces.
Marino Barovier's gallery for contemporary and historic studio glass and design, respected for its scholarship and museum collaborations.
notes.openai: A specialist platform commissioning and exhibiting contemporary artists who engage experimentally with glass and Venetian craft production.
A centrally located independent venue presenting rotating exhibitions by contemporary Italian and international artists.

galleries.name: Galleria d'Arte L'Occhio
galleries.address_hint: Dorsoduro 181, near Santa Maria della Salute

notes.anthropic: Long-established gallery showing contemporary painting, sculpture and glass by Italian and international artists.
notes.openai: A durable small gallery near the Salute known for modern and contemporary works by Italian, Venetian and international artists.

notes.anthropic: Mainz-based gallery's Venice space, showing concrete, minimal and light-based artists such as Mack, Morellet and Venet.

notes.openai: A gallery and publishing initiative valued for researched exhibitions on Venetian visual culture, photography and modern or contemporary artists.
The Venetian outpost of a national gallery network specializing in accessible blue-chip, street, pop and contemporary art.

galleries.name: Fondazione dell'Albero d'Oro – Palazzo Vendramin Grimani
galleries.address_hint: Palazzo Vendramin Grimani, Campo San Polo 2033

notes.anthropic: Restored palazzo staging carefully curated dialogues between contemporary artists and Venetian history.

names.anthropic: Fondazione dell'Albero d'Oro – Palazzo Vendramin Grimani

galleries.name: Ca' Foscari Esposizioni / Spazio Ca' Foscari Zattere

notes.anthropic: University exhibition spaces presenting research-based contemporary shows and Biennale collateral events open to the public.

names.anthropic: Ca' Foscari Esposizioni / Spazio Ca' Foscari Zattere

notes.openai: A distinctive curatorial gallery crossing contemporary art, sculpture, design and artist-made jewelry, with carefully researched thematic exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Historic gallery and publishing house founded by Carlo Cardazzo in 1942 — central to Spatialism and Italian video art — still active with its archive and editions.

notes.openai: A corporate art foundation presenting recurring contemporary exhibitions and commissioned installations in a dedicated Venetian palazzo.

notes.anthropic: Ghetto gallery combining contemporary painting and Judaica-related programming; long-standing presence in Cannaregio.

notes.openai: A permanent foundation venue supporting contemporary architecture, design and art exhibitions, including work by emerging practitioners.
An established Ghetto-area gallery offering a steady programme of contemporary painting, sculpture, photography and international group exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Flexible exhibition venue on the Zattere used for independent contemporary shows and Biennale-period projects.

notes.openai: An independent gallery especially attentive to photography, installation and cross-cultural contemporary projects.
A longstanding independent gallery supporting Venetian and Italian contemporary artists through regularly changing exhibitions.

notes.anthropic: Anglo-Venetian gallery of long standing, best known for the work of Geoffrey Humphries and figurative painters working in Venice.

notes.openai: A community-oriented Giudecca gallery providing public exhibition space for contemporary Venetian and visiting artists.
An intimate residency and exhibition initiative supporting artist-led experimentation and projects developed specifically in Venice.
The university’s public exhibition programme has presented substantial international contemporary-art projects, particularly during Biennale periods.

galleries.name: Combo Venezia
galleries.address_hint: Campo dei Gesuiti 4878, ex Convento dei Crociferi

notes.anthropic: Cultural hub in a former convent whose gallery hosts free contemporary exhibitions, screenings and residencies aimed at younger audiences.
Historic serigraphy workshop that doubles as an exhibition space, printing editions with international contemporary artists.

notes.openai: A commercial gallery notable for bringing contemporary glass, sculpture and collectible art into dialogue with Venice’s material traditions.

notes.anthropic: Mainland gallery with a young, digitally engaged programme and a solid Italian fair presence; part of the wider Venetian scene.

notes.openai: A small, longstanding gallery recognized for editions, optical and kinetic work, and carefully selected modern and contemporary artists.

notes.anthropic: Research-minded mainland gallery supporting emerging Veneto artists with a curatorial, non-commercial-first approach.

notes.openai: ITS LIQUID’s permanent presentation space hosts frequent open-call and internationally sourced exhibitions across art, architecture and design.

notes.anthropic: Corporate-backed art hub opened 2025 in a restored palazzo, offering exhibitions, a residency and public programming.

notes.openai: A centrally placed independent gallery with decades of activity in modern, contemporary and glass-related art.

notes.anthropic: Veteran central gallery handling modern and contemporary Italian painting and sculpture with regular seasonal shows.

notes.openai: A longstanding local gallery maintaining a public programme of Italian figurative and contemporary art in a prominent cultural district.

notes.anthropic: Established San Marco dealer combining 20th-century Italian art with contemporary figurative painting and glass.

notes.openai: A historic artists’ association and exhibition venue that continues to provide public visibility for contemporary practitioners in Venice.
